audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer puts Karma's root on her Q. mid says "her level-6 Mantra-Q root window", whys[4] "Mantra-Q root-slow burst", spikes[0] "Mantra-Q (RQ) root-slow burst window", spikes[1] "Karma's Mantra-Q roots", wants.you[2] "Bait the RQ root", wants.foe[0] "Land Mantra-Q (RQ) root-slow". Focused Resolve is never named anywhere in the content layer.
audit.why: Riot's text: Inner Flame (Q) "deals damage upon hitting an enemy unit" and the Mantra bonus adds "a cataclysm which deals damage after a short delay" — damage and a slow, no root. The root is Focused Resolve (W): "Karma creates a tether... If the tether is not broken, the enemy will be rooted and damaged again." A Zac player watching her Q for a root will eat the root every time, and will also miss the actual counterplay, which is breaking the tether.
audit.corrected: The root is Focused Resolve (W), 12s flat at 675 range, and it only lands if the tether survives.

audit.whatIsWrong: The tether-break counterplay appears only in the full layer and nowhere in the content layer, which tells the player to "bait or dodge the RQ root" instead.
audit.why: Because the root only fires if the tether is not broken, Zac has a real out: Elastic Slingshot is a long self-launch, so committing it into or away from her breaks the link before the root resolves. That converts her main CC from something to be feared into something with a specific, actionable answer.
audit.corrected: Break the tether — with Slingshot distance or line of sight — and the root never resolves.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places treat level 6 as Karma's power spike: mid ("her level-6 Mantra-Q root window swings that one beat back to her"), whys[4] ("Karma's level-6 Mantra-Q root-slow burst reclaims the lane"), spikes[0] ("The one danger is her level-6 Mantra-Q"), spikes[1] ("At 6 Karma's Mantra-Q roots and heavily chunks you").
audit.why: Riot's text for Mantra is explicit: "Mantra is available at level 1 and does not require a skill point." Karma has had it the entire lane. Level 6 gives her a rank (40s down to 38s) and nothing else, while it gives Zac Let's Bounce! outright. The entry has the one genuinely one-sided level in the lane pointed the wrong way — and it also means her level 1 is stronger than the entry explains, because she can Mantra-Q from the first wave.
audit.corrected: Mantra is hers from level 1, so 6 is your spike, not hers — and her level-1 RQ is the early threat.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Track her Mantra cooldown religiously" is the only cooldown guidance, with no number attached anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Mantra is 40s at rank 1 and Focused Resolve is 12s flat at every rank. Those two numbers are what "track it" actually means, and they point at different things: the 12s is how often the root is available, the 40s is how often it is a real threat rather than a chip.
audit.corrected: Mantra 40s at rank 1; Focused Resolve 12s flat at every rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is absent from both layers.
audit.why: Riot's Mantra bonus on Focused Resolve: "Karma strengthens the link, healing herself and extending the root duration." So her strongest CC is also her sustain, and _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup for needs-antiheal on that exact ability. Against Zac's grinding damage pattern that healing is what turns an even trade into a lost one.
audit.corrected: Mantra-W heals her while extending the root — Grievous Wounds is worth a slot.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] says Karma has "no hard CC left" at two-plus items.
audit.why: Focused Resolve is a root on a flat 12s cooldown and it never goes away. What is true is that it is her only hard CC and Zac out-durables one root — which is a different and more useful statement.
audit.corrected: She keeps one root all game; with two items you out-durable it.

notes:
The two layers were already telling different stories here. The full layer correctly builds the whole matchup around Focused Resolve; the content layer never mentions it once and attributes the root to Mantra-Q instead. Everything I changed on the content side moves it onto the full layer's (correct) footing rather than inventing a third version.

I moved win[4] from Karma to Skill rather than to Zac. Karma gains nothing genuinely new at 6 — Mantra is hers from level 1 — while Zac gains Let's Bounce!, so "Karma wins level 6" cannot stand. But at 49.69% over 320 games (the largest sample in this slice) a chart reading Zac 5 / Karma 1 / Skill 1 would overstate the lane, so Skill is the honest value.

phases[i].side, diff and diffRating are below the applier's 12-character minimum for a full-layer "before", so the full layer still shows Karma at Level 6 even after this. That stage needs the same treatment by whatever mechanism can write short fields.
